# ARGUS 2027 build progress

The build session's log. Feature and gate status live in `docs/build/features.json`; read them with `python3 tools/build_ledger.py summary`. The live copies of both files are on the integration branch `platform/build-2027`; `main` keeps the starting copies until the build ends. How the session works is in `docs/build/SESSION.md`.

## Needs a person

Steps the session cannot do. The session adds a row whenever a feature leaves one.

| For | What | Who |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DAT lane, PLT-04 | Training data: Roboflow key rotated, 2026 full-frame export, `.pt` weights and ONNX, field data days. Lifting the hold is the lead's call | Lead |
| CEN-03 | Buy and fit the downward rangefinder (TFmini Plus or TFmini-S) | Lead |
| REC-4, REC-9 | Recovery mechanism and its numbers: capture half-widths, hook position, suspension length, hover throttle with 1 and 2 kg | Mechanical team |
| PLT-05 | Wire an LED to a Jetson GPIO in the camera's view | Lead |
| SIM-10 | Tier D has no owner: someone runs the long suites weekly on the GPU desktop (`sim/run_scenarios.sh gates` today; the 4K stills and replay runs when SIM-05, SIM-09 and SIM-12 exist) | Lead to assign |
| SIM-10 | A club machine that never sleeps for nightly runs, and a GitHub token limited to issues. Then: log `gh` in with that token (or export it as `GH_TOKEN` for the job), pin an issue and set `ARGUS_NIGHTLY_ISSUE` to its number, and start `sim/nightly.sh` from cron or a systemd timer. Try `sim/nightly.sh --dry-run` first. It flies `origin/main`, so it has nothing to fly until wave 0 (the runner, `sim/run_scenarios.sh`) has landed on `main` | Lead |
| SIM-10 | Two edits to guardrail files the session may not touch. (1) `scripts/pr_checks.py`, `gate_tests`: change `c.path.startswith(("src/", "tools/"))` to `("src/", "tools/", "sim/")`, so a pull request that changes Python under `sim/` must change a test; add a test to `scripts/test/test_pr_checks.py` that a `sim/` Python change with no test change fails (the existing `test_non_src_python_needs_no_test` uses `scripts/helper.py` and still passes), and update the Tests row in CONTRIBUTING.md. Until this is done the wave-0 line "CI requires tests for `sim/`" is not met as written. (2) Fold the secret scan into the hygiene gate, as the spec says: call `secret_scan.findings(ctx)` from `gate_hygiene`, and scan staged lines in `run_staged` for `.githooks/pre-commit`. Today `scripts/check.sh` runs it as its own step, so `/ship`'s re-check of the real title and description (`python3 scripts/pr_checks.py`) does not scan them; only CI does. (3) Add the tier C line (run `sim/run_scenarios.sh smoke`, paste the table) to `.github/pull_request_template.md` | Lead |
| Wave 4 | Jetson on the bench, camera calibration per sensor mode, flight-controller parameters loaded, failsafes tested with the safety pilot | Lead |
| PLT-13, G6 | Any flight in the club simulator (`sim/gps/`), which a person starts | Lead |
| All | The organiser questions in FEATURES.md, "Open questions" | Lead |
| SIM-02, PLT-08, OPS-01 | Check every coordinate in `sim/sites/apollo_xi.yaml` against the organisers' field map (origin, ground elevation, runway, flight boundary, maximum height, takeoff point, compass rose, survey area), then set `verified: true`. They are placeholders | Lead |
| SIM-02 | Reword the SIM-02 pass line in FEATURES.md: a GUIDED waypoint outside the fence is refused by ArduPilot and causes no breach (see Decisions) | Lead |

## Decisions made during the build

Choices the specs did not settle, with the reason. Newest first.

| Date | Feature | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-10 | Tier A's list names tests for things that do not exist yet: wind (SIM-03), GPS conversions (SIM-04), payload bridge (SIM-06), replay `core` (SIM-09), dataset and registry tools and model parity (DAT lane). Each of those features registers its tests in `scripts/check.sh`; the coverage guard fails if one is left out | Nothing to run for them in wave 0 |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-10 | The secret-pattern rule is a new script, `scripts/secret_scan.py`, run by `scripts/check.sh` right after the PR gates. It reads the same changes through `pr_checks.load_context` and is waived by the same hygiene marker. The spec puts the rule inside the hygiene gate of `scripts/pr_checks.py` | The session may not edit `scripts/pr_checks.py` (a guardrail file; even copying it was refused). CI scans for secrets today; folding it into the gate is a person step |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-10 | "`pr_checks.py` counts `sim/` as code" is not done by the session: it is a one-line change in the same guardrail file, written out under "Needs a person". Until then `scripts/test/test_check_coverage.py` fails when any Python module under `sim/` is reached by no test (four thin ROS and MAVLink wrappers are listed as exempt, each with its reason), and when a test file is missing from `scripts/check.sh` | The per-pull-request rule belongs to the lead's gate. The whole-tree check is weaker: it catches a `sim/` module with no test at all, not a change to a tested module that comes without a test change |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-10 | Secret patterns: private-key headers, AWS, GitHub, Google, Slack and Hugging Face token formats, a password inside a URL, and a quoted literal with letters and digits assigned to a name containing api key, secret, token or password. Placeholders, environment-variable names and references are let through | The leak this answers was an API key assigned in a notebook cell. A generic entropy scan would flag commit hashes and coordinates |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-10 | Tier B is `sim/nightly.sh` (fresh worktree of `origin/main`, the `nightly` suite, `gh issue comment` on the issue in `ARGUS_NIGHTLY_ISSUE`); tier C is the `smoke` suite; tier D has no script of its own yet, only the `gates` suite | The ledger says wave 0 builds tier A and may write the tier B to D scripts; the 4K stills and replay that tier D names do not exist yet |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-11 | A gate's seeds and variants are fixed in `gates.yaml`; `sim/run_scenarios.sh G0 --variants off,on` is refused. To compare flags off with on, fly the gate's scenario by name with `--variants off,on`; the gate itself judges only its own flights | A gate's flights are part of its pass rule ("5/5", flags off); extra flights the check would ignore invite picking results |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-11 | Parts of pass lines the rules cannot check and the lanes owe in their scenarios: G1's two hold heights (6 m and 2 m), G5's coordinate error of up to 8 m and 5 m glitch mid-descent. Parts now encoded as rules: G5 at least ten flights and 8 of every 10, G6 five flights of each mission and one in moderate wind, G1 and G2 a run in each wind level. Judge limits a scenario could loosen (1.83 m, 7.62 m, the 1 m and 4 m tolerances) are pinned by rules on the score's `settings` | A rule reads a run's score and scenario manifest; a hold height or a glitch size is not in either yet. Nothing else stops a lane from leaving a condition out, so it is written down here |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-11 | The gates are data (`sim/scenarios/gates.yaml`) checked by `sim/gate.py`; each gate is also a runner suite (`sim/run_scenarios.sh G0`). G0 has its flights now. G1 to G6 have their rules written against the judges' outputs but no scenarios: the lane that builds a gate's scenarios adds them. Three rules name a metric no judge reports yet: G1 `details.hold_error_p95_m`, G5 `details.ended_safely`, G3 `details.impulse_ok` needs contact events | The spec gives each gate's pass line; the scenarios need wind, payload physics and the mission lanes. Writing the rules now fixes what each lane's judge must report |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-11 | A gate's verdict: FAIL if a flight is missing, did not finish, or an every-run rule is broken by a judged run; INVALID if a flight has only INVALID runs and nothing is already lost; the first run of a flight that counts is the one judged, so only an INVALID run can be flown again | "Don't round numbers into a pass": re-flying must not be a way to pick a better result |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-11 | How some pass lines are read as rules. G0 "5/5": every one of the five flights within 0.3 m. G4 "95% listed and IDs correct": correct markers over true markers, summed over the gate's runs. G5 "8/10": at least 8 runs scoring 0.5 points or more before the bonus (lifted, not released high, set down within 15.5 m). G6 "5/5": every waypoint of every flight | The table gives one line per gate; these are the closest checkable readings. Each is one line in `gates.yaml` |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | The wait for the sim's READY file (900 s by default, `READY_TIMEOUT_S`) is on the host's wall clock; every other duration of a run is in sim time | There is no sim clock until Gazebo is up, and the host script cannot read it |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | The recorder does not write `contact` events (the delivery impulse the judge reports and G3 needs). SIM-06, which builds the payload physics, owes them | A contact impulse needs a contact sensor on the payload, which does not exist until the payload is a real attached body |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | "On the ground" for ending a flight is the autopilot's landed state when it sends one, and otherwise the vehicle's true height being under 0.3 m while disarmed | The landed state is only streamed when something asks for it (the 2026 takeoff service does). A flight flown by `fence_check.py` never reported it, and the first such run ended only at its timeout |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07, SIM-02, SIM-08 | A scenario may name a `driver` (so far `fence_check`) that flies the vehicle in place of a mission launch, and a seventh judge, `geofence`, scores the SIM-02 pass line from true positions: 1 point if the autopilot reported the breach and left the commanded flight within 2 s of the true position crossing the fence, and stayed within 10 m. Scenario `geofence/breach` is in the `nightly` suite. It earns no autonomy bonus | SIM-02 owed a scored, true-pose run of its pass line, and no mission flies through a fence. The 1 Hz mode message can read a second late, so the autopilot's prompt breach report counts as the response, provided a home-or-stop mode follows within the 2 s limit plus that one second |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | The recorder also writes `mode` events (each flight-mode change), and `launch`, `end` and `clock` marks; the judges ignore what they do not know | The geofence judge needs the mode; the others make a trace readable |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | The recorder reads true poses and sim time straight from Gazebo with its Python bindings (already in the sim image), not through a ROS bridge. Bridging true poses to `/sim/truth/poses` is left to SIM-05, where the oracle detector needs it | `ros_gz_bridge` turns `Pose_V` into a TF message without model names in this version; Gazebo's own message has them |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | A scenario that asks for wind or GPS events is not flown and is reported INVALID with the reason, until `sim/wind.py` (SIM-03) and `sim/inject.py` (SIM-04) exist. The runner starts each with the run folder as its argument and stops it when the flight ends | A windy scenario flown calm would be reported as if it had wind |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | The real-time factor is averaged from arm to disarm, from clock marks the recorder writes every 5 s of sim time. The flight ends 5 s of sim time after a disarm on the ground that has lasted 3 s; arming must happen within 300 s of sim time | The sim idles at about 0.4 of real time on the ground before arming, which says nothing about the flight. The settle time lets a dropped payload come to rest |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | Human input is read from MAVProxy's MAVLink log after the flight: a command message or RC override from system id 255 inside the recording. A ground station asking for data (commands 410, 511, 512, 519, 520) does not count | MAVROS cannot see what a ground station sends; MAVProxy logs every sender. MAVProxy itself sends 410 at start-up |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-07 | Suites: `smoke` is one flags-off flight of `delivery/baseline`; `gates` is that scenario five times (G0), to be extended by the lanes; `nightly` is every scenario, seeds 1 to 3, off and on. The mission is launched with its launch file's own defaults, so the 2026 session logger runs as it did | The spec names the suites but not their contents |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | A scenario names the object its mission carries (`payload:`) and the one recovery must bring back (`bucket:`); only those become the judge's payload and bucket. Other packages and buckets are just on the field | Otherwise the loose package in `delivery/clutter` earned the delivery weight bonus, and would have been scored as the delivered package |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | A scenario with no `sun:` keeps the base world's light, the one the 2026 sim flew under; `sun: {elevation_deg, azimuth_deg}` replaces it | The flags-off baseline (G0) should see what the 2026 detector was measured with |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | The 2027 marker model (`build_marker_sdf`) is a black-and-white X plate with a seven-segment digit centred on a white field over the crossing, no underline; a marker with no digit is a 1.2 m boundary marker. The 2026 `build_bw_target_sdf` (digit off-centre, underlined) is left as it was | The spec says "digit centred in the X as the rules show"; the font and the 6/9 mark are organiser question 8. One builder to change when the answer comes |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | A scenario is built as variant `off` (every flag false, the 2026 behaviour) or `on` (the scenario's flags); flags are written only to the copies in the run folder. A mission flag must be declared under `features:` in the shipped sequence, a node flag under that node's `ros__parameters.features` in the shipped params file | The spec's rule that shipped YAML stays false, and the runner's off-against-on table (SIM-07) |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | `wind`, `gps_events` and `sensor_profile` are checked and passed to the runner in `scenario.json`, but nothing acts on them yet; the only sensor profile is `delivery` (the 2026 camera); the payload and bucket are loose bodies, not attached to the vehicle | Wind is SIM-03, GPS faults SIM-04, camera profiles SIM-05, payload joints SIM-06 |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | A scenario's `config` override must name a setting that exists in the shipped sequence; an object is placed with `at`, or `on_top_of` another object | A typo would otherwise be ignored by the mission. `on:` cannot be used as a YAML key: YAML reads it as `true` |
| 2026-11-15 | SIM-01 | Shipped scenarios: `delivery/baseline` and `drop/baseline` (the 2026 missions, bullseye 10 m east and 15 m north of the takeoff point as in the 2026 sim baseline), `delivery/clutter` (the same with every 2027 object on the field) and `waypoint_navigation/site_circuit` (an invented seven-point route inside the placeholder boundary) | The 2026 waypoint route is at last year's field; the lanes add their own scenarios |

Left for the lead: `pr_checks.py` counting `sim/` as code and holding the secret rule, the nightly machine and token, the PR template line, an owner for tier D.
